name: Zone-Read RB Draw Package
situation: 1st & 10, +25, tempo snap into a light nickel box before the defense can add a hat

summary.motive: Pair the zone-read's unblocked-end geometry with an RB delayed draw so the defense's box math commits to a play flowing one way while the ball hits a vacated gap going the other.
summary.keyDefender: Unblocked read-key DE and the WILL fitting the draw
summary.whyItWorks: The read forces the end to declare, and his crash — plus the linebackers' and sky safety's flow reads against the zone action — empties both the edge and the backside B-gap simultaneously; by the time the draw reveals itself, every hat is wrong-sided.
summary.failureMode: A disciplined end who stays home on the near-back and squeezes rather than crashes, letting the defense spill the draw to the WILL before the redirect can clear the hole.

beats.title: 1. The Unblocked Read Key
beats.text: Kelly's offensive line deliberately leaves the backside end untouched — LT hinges away from him. The QB presents the ball on a wide-zone ride and stares straight at that defender, whose next step decides where the ball goes.

beats.title: 2. Box Math Breaks
beats.text: The WDE crashes down on the give while WILL and the rolling SS trigger downhill with the zone flow. The defense now has seven hats chasing a play that's about to reverse direction — the box is mathematically wrong-sided.

beats.title: 3. The Draw Redirect
beats.text: RB gathers, plants, and takes the handoff back through the B-gap the crashing WDE just vacated — behind C and LG double-walls. Every defender who flowed right is now taking the longest possible angle to the ball.

beats.title: 4. Second Level, Wrong-Way Fits
beats.text: The WILL arrives at the hole a full beat after the back hits it, and the free safety — the only clean body — breaks down from 15 yards away. Kelly's tempo means this same geometry stress repeats on the very next snap.

relations.tell: RB presses wide-zone right for two steps, then sinks his hips and snaps back into the backside B-gap — the mid-play hip turn at the mesh point is the only visual cue.
